automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Include only public web sources published or visibly updated within the last 2 days relative to the run time. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, boundary-only, stale, upstream-only, or inaccessible candidates.

federation_policy.local_scope: AI-assisted development practice lens: context architecture, source workflows, durable instructions, agent operating practices, coding practices, retrieval and tool governance, verification, application harness patterns, governance, risk, and team adoption.
federation_policy.collector_boundary: Items name upstream-owned entities when useful, but only the local practice implication is retained for downstream ingest.

queries: site:github.blog/changelog "July 13, 2026" AI prompt injection code review

qualifying_findings.source_title: AI-coding agents spread through peer pressure, not mandates
qualifying_findings.summary: LeadDev reported that manager and peer visibility can increase trial of AI coding agents, but retention depends on workflow fit. The article also warned that AI-generated pull requests can create review pressure that encourages cursory approval.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Adoption guidance should separate experimentation norms from usage mandates and pair rollout pressure with review-capacity controls, outcome measures, and explicit safeguards against shallow review of AI-generated changes.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep organization and product background upstream; retain local notes about adoption pressure, workflow fit, and code-review capacity.

qualifying_findings.source_title: Should Developers Stop Reading AI-Generated Code? The Review Debate
qualifying_findings.summary: ExplainX framed the debate over reading every line of AI-generated code as a shift toward risk-based, evidence-driven review instead of all-or-nothing manual review.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Code-review guidance should define when line-by-line reading is mandatory, when tests/static analysis/runtime evidence can carry more weight, and how reviewers document risk-based acceptance for AI-authored changes.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep vendor background upstream; retain local practice implications for risk-tiered review policies and evidence requirements.

qualifying_findings.source_title: IBM Bob Gets Multi-Agent Muscle and a Cost Dashboard for Enterprise Coding
qualifying_findings.summary: DevOps.com reported that IBM Bob added multi-agent coordination, built-in spend tracking, and prebuilt workflows for mainframe COBOL, IBM i, and large Java modernization.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Enterprise agent workflow guidance should track multi-agent work as a coordinated operating model with cost telemetry and modernization-specific acceptance gates, not just as generic coding assistance.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Route product and vendor details upstream; keep local notes about multi-agent coordination, spend visibility, and modernization workflow controls.

qualifying_findings.source_title: AI-generated code has made security debt a governance problem
qualifying_findings.summary: CyberScoop argued that approving AI coding tools is insufficient governance; organizations need records of where AI-generated code enters, which policies and tests applied, what issues were found, and what fixes were made.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Governance pages should treat AI-authored code as an auditable source class with traceability from generation through review, test evidence, remediation, and policy decision records.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep publisher and broad security commentary upstream; retain local practice implications for audit logs, source tracking, policy evidence, and remediation records.

qualifying_findings.source_title: How SonarQube enables companies in regulated industries to accelerate innovation with AI
qualifying_findings.summary: SonarSource described AI-assisted development in regulated industries as an agent-centric cycle of guiding, verifying, and solving across generation, CI/CD verification, and maintenance loops.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Regulated-team guidance should frame AI-assisted development as a lifecycle control system where organizational standards guide agents before work begins and independent verification gates run before code reaches the main codebase.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Route product and vendor positioning upstream; retain local notes about lifecycle controls, independent verification, and regulated-industry rollout.

qualifying_findings.source_title: The Frontend Verification Gap in AI-Assisted Development
qualifying_findings.summary: O'Reilly described a frontend verification gap where AI-generated UI can compile and render while still failing realistic user conditions such as accessibility, keyboard behavior, focus management, state changes, loading and error handling, and end-to-end task completion.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Verification-loop guidance should require UI acceptance checks beyond compilation and screenshots, including task completion, accessibility, focus, state, error, and loading behavior for AI-generated frontend work.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep publisher background upstream; retain local implications for frontend acceptance gates and user-flow verification.

qualifying_findings.source_title: 99.9% of fixable AI vulnerabilities remain unpatched
qualifying_findings.summary: Help Net Security summarized Orca Security findings that production agent frameworks, RAG pipelines, default permissions, weak logging, exposed keys, and missing runtime separation are creating an operational AI security layer with new blast-radius concerns.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Tool and RAG governance should include inventory, permissions, runtime separation, credential hygiene, logging, and blast-radius review for agents and retrieval systems that touch codebases or enterprise data.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep report and infrastructure background upstream; retain local notes about permission defaults, logging, separation, and credential controls for AI-assisted development systems.

qualifying_findings.summary: Parallel's product post included an agent-facing setup instruction that tells agents to read a public agents.md file and install or configure the service, alongside CLI and MCP entrypoints.
qualifying_findings.practice_relevance: Durable-instruction guidance should treat public agent-onboarding snippets as untrusted source instructions that require user approval, package-install review, and tool-permission checks before execution.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Route product coverage upstream; retain local practice implications for external AGENTS-style instructions, installation prompts, and MCP/tool permission review.
